name.text: Subject Overlap Analysis in Student Survey

questiontext.text:
In a survey involving \({@Tot@}\) students at a school, it was found that \({@num_M@}\) study Mathematics, \({@num_P@}\) study Physics and \({@num_C@}\) study Chemistry, \({@num_mnp@}\) study Mathematics and Physics, \({@num_pnc@}\) study Physics and Chemistry, \({@num_mnc@}\) study Chemistry and Mathematics and \({@num_n@}\) none of the subjects. Find the number of students who study all the three subjects.

The number of students studying all the three subjects is [[input:ans1]]. [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

So, \(n(U)={@Tot@},\)

\(n(M)={@num_M@},\,n(P)={@num_P@}\)

\(n(C)={@num_P@}, \, n(M \cap P)={@num_mnp@}, \, n(P \cap C)={@num_pnc@}\)

\(n(M \cap C)={@num_mnc@}, \, n(M \cup P \cup C)^{\prime}={@num_n@}\)

Therefore \(n(M \cup P \cup C)^{\prime}=n(U)-n(M \cup P \cup C)\)

\( \implies {@num_n@}={@Tot@}-n(M \cup P \cup C)\)

\( \implies n(M \cup P \cup C)={@Tot-num_n@}\)

\( \implies n(M \cup P \cup C)=n(M)+n(P)+n(C)-n(M \cap P)-n(P \cap C)-n(C \cap M)+n(C \cap M \cap P)\)

Therefore \({@Tot-num_n@}={@num_M@}+{@num_P@}+{@num_C@}-{@num_mnp@}-{@num_pnc@}-{@num_mnc@}+n(C \cap M \cap P)\)

\(\implies {@Tot-num_n@}={@num_M+num_P+num_C@}-{@num_mnp+num_pnc+num_mnc@}+n(C \cap M \cap P)\)

\( \implies n(C \cap M \cap P)={@Tot-num_n+(num_mnp+num_pnc+num_mnc)-(num_M+num_P+num_C)@}\)

This question requires the student to decipher the overlapping study preferences of students surveyed at a school. By analyzing the given data on dual subject studies and those opting for none, the challenge is to determine the precise number of students who engage in the study of all three subjects.
